*Program for the creation of the longitudinal county to place crosswalk for UMF predictors*

This program was originally a chunk in `11_housing-affordability/ratio_housing_affordable_available.qmd` and was moved here so the crosswalk doesn't depend on rendering the housing affordability metric (#648). It addresses two issues:

-   Connecticut counties are replaced by planning regions in 2022.
-   A pre-2020 county to place crosswalk is needed for back-filling.

It writes two files to `geographic-crosswalks/data/`:

-   `geocorr2022_county_place_2022_onwards.csv`: the 2020-2021 county to place crosswalk with the Connecticut counties replaced by the planning regions. Read by `11_housing-affordability`.
-   `county_place_crosswalk_longitudinal.csv`: one row per county-place pair and year, 2010-2029. Read by `23_safety-from-crime` and `24_just-policing`.

Primary data derived from the University of Missouri's [geographic correspondence engine](https://mcdc.missouri.edu/applications/geocorr.html).

## Housekeeping

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(here)
```

## Connecticut planning regions

Obtain a dedicated Connecticut planning region to place crosswalk from GeoCorr:

*Crosswalk type:* Planning Regions to Places
*States:* Connecticut
*Source geography:* 2022 Connecticut Planning Region
*Target geography:* 2020 Places
*Weighting variable:* Population (2020 census)
*Output Options:* CSV w/ second allocation factor (AFACT2)

```{r}
## Read in the dedicated crosswalk for CT Planning regions
ct_planning_region_crosswalk = read_csv(
  here("geographic-crosswalks", "data", "geocorr2022_ct_planning_region_to_place.csv"),
  skip = 1) %>%
  select(
    countyfip = `Connecticut planning region`,
    CountyName = `Connecticut planning region name`,
    state = `State code`,
    place = `Place code`,
    PlaceName = `Place name`,
    stab = `State abbr.`,
    population = `Total population (2020 Census)`,
    afact = `ctregion-to-place allocation factor`,
    afact2 = `place-to-ctregion allocation factor`) %>%
  mutate(population_vintage = 2020)

## Read in the existing county-place crosswalk
county_place_crosswalk_2020_2021 = read_csv(
  here("geographic-crosswalks", "data", "geocorr2022_county_place_2020_2021.csv")) %>%
    mutate(
      state = str_pad(as.numeric(state), side = "left", width = 2, pad = "0"),
      place = str_pad(as.numeric(place), side = "left", width = 5, pad = "0"),
      countyfip = str_pad(as.character(countyfip), side = "left", width = 5, pad = "0"),
      population_vintage = 2020,
      crosswalk_period = "2020-2021") %>%
  rename(population = pop20) %>%
  select(-county)

## all places should be in both crosswalks
stopifnot(
  county_place_crosswalk_2020_2021 %>%
    filter(state == "09", !place %in% ct_planning_region_crosswalk$place) %>%
    nrow == 0)

## remove old CT counties, add new CT planning regions
county_place_crosswalk_2022_2029 = county_place_crosswalk_2020_2021 %>%
  filter(state != "09") %>%
  bind_rows(ct_planning_region_crosswalk) %>%
  arrange(countyfip, PlaceName) %>%
  mutate(crosswalk_period = "2022-2029")

## there should be exactly nine distinct county-level records for the state of CT
stopifnot(
  county_place_crosswalk_2022_2029 %>%
    filter(state == "09") %>%
    distinct(CountyName) %>%
    nrow() == 9)

county_place_crosswalk_2022_2029 %>%
  write_csv(here("geographic-crosswalks", "data", "geocorr2022_county_place_2022_onwards.csv"))
```

## Pre-2020 crosswalk

*Crosswalk type:* County to Place
*States:* All
*Source geography:* 2014 Counties
*Target geography:* 2014 Places
*Weighting variable:* Population (2010 census)
*Output Options:* CSV w/ second allocation factor (AFACT2)

```{r}
county_place_crosswalk_pre_2020 = read_csv(
  here("geographic-crosswalks", "data", "geocorr2018_county_place_2014_thru_2019.csv"),
  skip = 1) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename_with( ~ str_remove_all(.x, "x2014_|_2014$|14")) %>%
  select(
    countyfip = county_code,
    CountyName = county_name,
    state = state_code,
    place,
    PlaceName = place_name,
    stab = state_abbreviation,
    population = population_2010,
    afact = county_to_placefp_allocation_factor,
    afact2 = placefp_to_county_allocation_factor) %>%
  mutate(
    population_vintage = 2010,
    crosswalk_period = "pre-2020")

## this crosswalk is from 2014 vintage geographies, but effective beginning in 2018
## we have a new city - South Fulton GA
## we add the records from the post-2020
```

## Longitudinal crosswalk

```{r}
crosswalk_years = tibble(
  year = c(2010:2029),
  crosswalk_period = c(rep("pre-2020", 10), rep("2020-2021", 2), rep("2022-2029", 8)))

county_place_crosswalk_longitudinal = bind_rows(
  county_place_crosswalk_pre_2020,
  county_place_crosswalk_2020_2021,
  county_place_crosswalk_2022_2029) %>%
  left_join(crosswalk_years, by = "crosswalk_period", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  filter(stab != "PR")

## there should be 20 years per county
stopifnot(
  county_place_crosswalk_longitudinal %>%
    filter(countyfip == "01001") %>%
    distinct(year) %>%
    nrow == 20)
```

## Checks

Compare the number of counties and places per year with `county-populations.csv` and `place-populations.csv`.

```{r}
place_populations = read_csv(here("geographic-crosswalks", "data", "place-populations.csv")) %>%
  mutate(place_fip = str_c(state, place))

county_populations = read_csv(here("geographic-crosswalks", "data", "county-populations.csv")) %>%
  mutate(county_fip = str_c(state, county))

county_benchmarking = county_place_crosswalk_longitudinal %>%
  group_by(year, crosswalk_period) %>%
  summarize(
    distinct_counties = n_distinct(countyfip)) %>%
  left_join(
    county_populations %>%
      group_by(year) %>%
      summarize(distinct_counties_benchmark = n_distinct(county_fip))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(distinct_counties_benchmark), distinct_counties != distinct_counties_benchmark)

stopifnot(
  nrow(county_benchmarking) == 0)

place_benchmark = county_place_crosswalk_longitudinal %>%
  mutate(place_fip = str_c(state, place)) %>%
  filter(
    ## addressing South Fulton GA -- due to crosswalk availability, we don't
    ## produce estimates for South Fulton for these years
    place_fip %in% place_populations$place_fip,
    !(str_detect(PlaceName, "South Fulton") & year %in% c(2018:2021))) %>%
  group_by(year, crosswalk_period) %>%
  summarize(
    distinct_places = n_distinct(place_fip)) %>%
  left_join(
    place_populations %>%
      group_by(year) %>%
      summarize(distinct_places_benchmark = n_distinct(place_fip))) %>%
  mutate(
    distinct_places_benchmark = case_when(
      ## addressing South Fulton GA -- due to crosswalk availability, we don't
      ## produce estimates for South Fulton for these years
      year < 2022 & year > 2017 ~ distinct_places_benchmark - 1,
      TRUE ~ distinct_places_benchmark)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(distinct_places_benchmark), distinct_places != distinct_places_benchmark)

stopifnot(
  nrow(place_benchmark) == 0)
```

## Write file

Some place names are missing (and corresponding place codes are effectively `NA`). This is fine. These are where counties don't overlap with places. We retain these because there are a few (n = ~10) counties that don't overlap with any places, and if we drop these, we can't benchmark to our total expected county population numbers as easily/accurately.

```{r}
write_csv(county_place_crosswalk_longitudinal, here("geographic-crosswalks", "data", "county_place_crosswalk_longitudinal.csv"))
```
